package ap

// ddsonic contract helper: a synthetic access point. Like ap_helper.go.txt,
// this file exists only in the overlay the contract runner builds over a
// staged copy of go-librespot. It listens on loopback TCP and answers the
// SDK's real handshake (key exchange, challenge, login), so that the real
// Accesspoint, its receive loop and its reconnect run against a real socket
// that a test can close from the peer's side.
//
// The SDK verifies the server's key-exchange signature against a key of its
// own package. The fake signs with a key it generates, and puts that key in
// the package's variable for as long as it is open; Close puts the SDK's key
// back. One fake is open at a time, and no test using one runs in parallel.

import (
	"context"
	"crypto"
	"crypto/hmac"
	"crypto/rand"
	"crypto/rsa"
	"crypto/sha1"
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net"
	"sync"
	"time"

	librespot "github.com/devgianlu/go-librespot"
	"github.com/devgianlu/go-librespot/dh"
	pb "github.com/devgianlu/go-librespot/proto/spotify"
	"google.golang.org/protobuf/proto"
)

// DDSonicFakeAP is the synthetic access point.
type DDSonicFakeAP struct {
	ln      net.Listener
	key     *rsa.PrivateKey
	sdkKey  *rsa.PublicKey
	conns   chan *DDSonicFakeConn
	closing chan struct{}
	once    sync.Once

	mu     sync.Mutex
	hold   chan struct{} // while set, a new connection's handshake waits
	refuse bool          // while set, a login is answered with a failure
	logins int
	all    []net.Conn
}

var ddsonicFakeOpen sync.Mutex

// DDSonicContractFakeAP starts a synthetic access point on loopback.
func DDSonicContractFakeAP() (*DDSonicFakeAP, error) {
	key, err := rsa.GenerateKey(rand.Reader, 2048)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	ddsonicFakeOpen.Lock() // until Close: the package's key is this fake's
	f := &DDSonicFakeAP{ln: ln, key: key, sdkKey: serverSigPubKey, conns: make(chan *DDSonicFakeConn, 16), closing: make(chan struct{})}
	serverSigPubKey = &key.PublicKey
	go f.accept()
	return f, nil
}

// Close stops the fake, closes its connections and restores the SDK's key.
func (f *DDSonicFakeAP) Close() {
	f.once.Do(func() {
		close(f.closing)
		_ = f.ln.Close()
		f.mu.Lock()
		for _, c := range f.all {
			_ = c.Close()
		}
		f.mu.Unlock()
		serverSigPubKey = f.sdkKey
		ddsonicFakeOpen.Unlock()
	})
}

// Connect is a real access point, authenticated against the fake. Its
// receive loop has not been started: that is the caller's to do, or not.
func (f *DDSonicFakeAP) Connect(ctx context.Context) (*Accesspoint, error) {
	addr := f.ln.Addr().String()
	a := NewAccesspoint(&librespot.NullLogger{}, func(context.Context) string { return addr }, "ddsonic-contract")
	if err := a.ConnectStored(ctx, "contract-user", []byte("contract-stored-credential")); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return a, nil
}

// Hold makes the handshake of every connection accepted from now on wait
// until release is called: a reconnect that has begun and cannot finish.
func (f *DDSonicFakeAP) Hold() (release func()) {
	gate := make(chan struct{})
	f.mu.Lock()
	f.hold = gate
	f.mu.Unlock()
	var once sync.Once
	return func() {
		once.Do(func() {
			f.mu.Lock()
			f.hold = nil
			f.mu.Unlock()
			close(gate)
		})
	}
}

// Refuse makes every login from now on fail, as a server that rejects the
// credential does, until undo is called.
func (f *DDSonicFakeAP) Refuse() (undo func()) {
	f.mu.Lock()
	f.refuse = true
	f.mu.Unlock()
	return func() {
		f.mu.Lock()
		f.refuse = false
		f.mu.Unlock()
	}
}

// Logins is how many connections have completed their login.
func (f *DDSonicFakeAP) Logins() int {
	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	return f.logins
}

// Next is the next connection to complete its login, or nil after d.
func (f *DDSonicFakeAP) Next(d time.Duration) *DDSonicFakeConn {
	select {
	case c := <-f.conns:
		return c
	case <-time.After(d):
		return nil
	}
}

func (f *DDSonicFakeAP) accept() {
	for {
		conn, err := f.ln.Accept()
		if err != nil {
			return
		}
		f.mu.Lock()
		f.all = append(f.all, conn)
		hold := f.hold
		f.mu.Unlock()
		go func() {
			if hold != nil {
				select {
				case <-hold:
				case <-f.closing:
					return
				}
			}
			c, err := f.handshake(conn)
			if err != nil {
				_ = conn.Close()
				return
			}
			f.mu.Lock()
			f.logins++
			f.mu.Unlock()
			go c.read()
			f.conns <- c
		}()
	}
}

// handshake is the server's side of Accesspoint.connect.
func (f *DDSonicFakeAP) handshake(conn net.Conn) (*DDSonicFakeConn, error) {
	_ = conn.SetDeadline(time.Now().Add(10 * time.Second))
	defer func() { _ = conn.SetDeadline(time.Time{}) }()

	// ClientHello: two hello bytes, a length that counts them and itself,
	// and the message. Every byte both ways is part of the challenge.
	var exchanged []byte
	head := make([]byte, 6)
	if _, err := io.ReadFull(conn, head); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	size := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(head[2:])
	if size < 6 || size > 4096 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("fake access point: a hello of %d bytes", size)
	}
	body := make([]byte, size-6)
	if _, err := io.ReadFull(conn, body); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	exchanged = append(append(exchanged, head...), body...)
	var hello pb.ClientHello
	if err := proto.Unmarshal(body, &hello); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	keys, err := dh.NewDiffieHellman()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	gs := keys.PublicKeyBytes()
	digest := sha1.Sum(gs)
	sig, err := rsa.SignPKCS1v15(rand.Reader, f.key, crypto.SHA1, digest[:])
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	nonce := make([]byte, 16)
	_, _ = rand.Read(nonce)
	resp, err := proto.Marshal(&pb.APResponseMessage{Challenge: &pb.APChallenge{
		LoginCryptoChallenge: &pb.LoginCryptoChallengeUnion{DiffieHellman: &pb.LoginCryptoDiffieHellmanChallenge{
			Gs: gs, ServerSignatureKey: proto.Int32(0), GsSignature: sig,
		}},
		FingerprintChallenge: &pb.FingerprintChallengeUnion{},
		PowChallenge:         &pb.PoWChallengeUnion{},
		CryptoChallenge:      &pb.CryptoChallengeUnion{},
		ServerNonce:          nonce,
	}})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	framed := binary.BigEndian.AppendUint32(nil, uint32(4+len(resp)))
	framed = append(framed, resp...)
	if _, err := conn.Write(framed); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	exchanged = append(exchanged, framed...)

	shared := keys.Exchange(hello.GetLoginCryptoHello().GetDiffieHellman().GetGc())
	macData := make([]byte, 0, sha1.Size*5)
	mac := hmac.New(sha1.New, shared)
	for i := byte(1); i < 6; i++ {
		mac.Reset()
		mac.Write(exchanged)
		mac.Write([]byte{i})
		macData = mac.Sum(macData)
	}
	mac = hmac.New(sha1.New, macData[:20])
	mac.Write(exchanged)

	// ClientResponsePlaintext: the client's proof that it has the secret.
	var plain pb.ClientResponsePlaintext
	if err := readMessage(conn, 4096, &plain); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if !hmac.Equal(plain.GetLoginCryptoResponse().GetDiffieHellman().GetHmac(), mac.Sum(nil)) {
		return nil, errors.New("fake access point: the client's challenge response is wrong")
	}

	// The client sends with macData[20:52] and receives with [52:84].
	enc := newShannonConn(conn, macData[52:84], macData[20:52])
	typ, _, err := enc.receivePacket(context.Background())
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if typ != PacketTypeLogin {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("fake access point: %v where a login was expected", typ)
	}
	f.mu.Lock()
	refuse := f.refuse
	f.mu.Unlock()
	if refuse {
		failed, _ := proto.Marshal(&pb.APLoginFailed{ErrorCode: pb.ErrorCode_BadCredentials.Enum()})
		_ = enc.sendPacket(context.Background(), PacketTypeAuthFailure, failed)
		return nil, errors.New("fake access point: login refused")
	}
	reusable := make([]byte, 24)
	_, _ = rand.Read(reusable)
	welcome, err := proto.Marshal(&pb.APWelcome{
		CanonicalUsername:           proto.String("contract-user"),
		AccountTypeLoggedIn:         pb.AccountType_Spotify.Enum(),
		CredentialsTypeLoggedIn:     pb.AccountType_Spotify.Enum(),
		ReusableAuthCredentialsType: pb.AuthenticationType_AUTHENTICATION_STORED_SPOTIFY_CREDENTIALS.Enum(),
		ReusableAuthCredentials:     reusable,
	})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if err := enc.sendPacket(context.Background(), PacketTypeAPWelcome, welcome); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return &DDSonicFakeConn{conn: conn, enc: enc, Packets: make(chan Packet, 64)}, nil
}

// DDSonicFakeConn is the fake's end of one authenticated connection.
type DDSonicFakeConn struct {
	conn net.Conn
	enc  *shannonConn
	// Packets is what the client sent, in order. It is closed when the
	// connection can no longer be read.
	Packets chan Packet
}

func (c *DDSonicFakeConn) read() {
	defer close(c.Packets)
	for {
		typ, payload, err := c.enc.receivePacket(context.Background())
		if err != nil {
			return
		}
		c.Packets <- Packet{Type: typ, Payload: payload}
	}
}

// Send sends the client one packet.
func (c *DDSonicFakeConn) Send(typ PacketType, payload []byte) error {
	return c.enc.sendPacket(context.Background(), typ, payload)
}

// PeerClose closes the connection from the access point's side as the
// client first sees it: the server's FIN arrives and the client's socket is
// in CLOSE_WAIT. The server's end still reads, as a remote peer's reset has
// not yet come back, so what the client writes afterwards is seen in
// Packets, and is never answered.
func (c *DDSonicFakeConn) PeerClose() error {
	tcp, ok := c.conn.(*net.TCPConn)
	if !ok {
		return errors.New("fake access point: not a TCP connection")
	}
	return tcp.CloseWrite()
}

// Wait is the next packet of the given type the client sent, skipping
// others, or false after d or when the connection ended.
func (c *DDSonicFakeConn) Wait(typ PacketType, d time.Duration) (Packet, bool) {
	deadline := time.After(d)
	for {
		select {
		case pkt, ok := <-c.Packets:
			if !ok {
				return Packet{}, false
			}
			if pkt.Type == typ {
				return pkt, true
			}
		case <-deadline:
			return Packet{}, false
		}
	}
}

// AnswerKey answers a key request with key: the request's sequence number
// (its last six bytes are the sequence and a zero word) and the key.
func (c *DDSonicFakeConn) AnswerKey(req Packet, key []byte) error {
	if req.Type != PacketTypeRequestKey || len(req.Payload) < 6 {
		return errors.New("fake access point: not a key request")
	}
	seq := req.Payload[len(req.Payload)-6 : len(req.Payload)-2]
	return c.Send(PacketTypeAesKey, append(append([]byte{}, seq...), key...))
}

// ddsonicGatedConn is a client connection whose reads wait for a test, and
// whose writes are reported to it.
type ddsonicGatedConn struct {
	net.Conn
	open   chan struct{}
	writes chan error
}

func (c *ddsonicGatedConn) Read(b []byte) (int, error) {
	<-c.open
	return c.Conn.Read(b)
}

func (c *ddsonicGatedConn) Write(b []byte) (int, error) {
	n, err := c.Conn.Write(b)
	select {
	case c.writes <- err:
	default:
	}
	return n, err
}

// DDSonicContractGateReads holds every read of a's current connection until
// release is called, and reports the result of each write on writes. It is
// the barrier that orders a write before the receive loop's first read. It
// is for an access point whose receive loop has not started.
func DDSonicContractGateReads(a *Accesspoint) (release func(), writes <-chan error) {
	a.connMu.Lock()
	defer a.connMu.Unlock()
	g := &ddsonicGatedConn{Conn: a.conn, open: make(chan struct{}), writes: make(chan error, 16)}
	a.conn = g
	a.encConn.conn = g
	var once sync.Once
	return func() { once.Do(func() { close(g.open) }) }, g.writes
}

// DDSonicContractForgetWelcome makes a's next reconnect fail for good, as
// one that has used up its retries does: the receive loop then closes the
// access point itself.
func DDSonicContractForgetWelcome(a *Accesspoint) {
	a.connMu.Lock()
	defer a.connMu.Unlock()
	a.welcome = nil
}

// DDSonicWriteGate passes a connection's writes through until it is armed
// (then every write waits, holding the connection's send lock, until
// Release) or told to fail (then every write fails, writing nothing, until
// Release).
type DDSonicWriteGate struct {
	net.Conn
	mu      sync.Mutex
	held    chan struct{}
	entered chan struct{}
	fail    error
}

func (g *DDSonicWriteGate) Write(b []byte) (int, error) {
	g.mu.Lock()
	if g.fail != nil {
		err := g.fail
		g.mu.Unlock()
		return 0, err
	}
	held, entered := g.held, g.entered
	if entered != nil {
		g.entered = nil
		close(entered)
	}
	g.mu.Unlock()
	if held != nil {
		<-held
	}
	return g.Conn.Write(b)
}

// Arm holds every write from now on; entered is closed when the first one
// is held.
func (g *DDSonicWriteGate) Arm() (entered <-chan struct{}) {
	g.mu.Lock()
	defer g.mu.Unlock()
	e := make(chan struct{})
	g.held, g.entered = make(chan struct{}), e
	return e
}

// Fail makes every write from now on fail with err, writing nothing.
func (g *DDSonicWriteGate) Fail(err error) {
	g.mu.Lock()
	defer g.mu.Unlock()
	g.fail = err
}

// Release lets the held writes, and every later one, through.
func (g *DDSonicWriteGate) Release() {
	g.mu.Lock()
	defer g.mu.Unlock()
	if g.held != nil {
		close(g.held)
	}
	g.held, g.entered, g.fail = nil, nil, nil
}

// DDSonicContractGateWrites puts a write gate, open, on a's current
// connection. It is for an access point whose receive loop has not started.
func DDSonicContractGateWrites(a *Accesspoint) *DDSonicWriteGate {
	a.connMu.Lock()
	defer a.connMu.Unlock()
	g := &DDSonicWriteGate{Conn: a.conn}
	a.conn = g
	a.encConn.conn = g
	return g
}
